binders: A Fintype structure on ι, making ι finite.
An IsProbabilityMeasure instance for μ, so μ(Ω) = 1.
A family B : ι → Ω → Bool of Boolean-valued functions.
hypotheses: For every i : ι, the function B i : Ω → Bool is measurable, where Bool has the discrete (top) measurable space.
The indexed family of functions B is mutually independent under μ.
For every i : ι, the pushforward measure map (B i) μ is exactly the measure associated with the Bernoulli(1/2) PMF on Bool; equivalently, each B i is fair with μ(B i = true) = μ(B i = false) = 1/2.
The finite cardinality card ι is strictly positive.
conclusions: The real-valued μ-measure of the event that the sum over all i : ι of the indicator 1_{B i ω = true} is at least (3/4) card ι is at most exp(-(card ι)/8).
mathematical_definitions: For b : Bool, define I(b) = 1 if b = true and I(b) = 0 otherwise.
Let n = card ι; the hypothesis 0 < n makes the finite index type nonempty.
For ω : Ω, the real sum Σ_{i∈ι} I(B i ω) equals the number of indices whose Boolean value is true.
The common marginal law is the fair Bernoulli law on Bool, assigning probability 1/2 to true and 1/2 to false.
The event in the conclusion is {ω ∈ Ω | Σ_{i∈ι} I(B i ω) ≥ (3/4)n}.
Measure.real converts μ of that event from an extended nonnegative real to a real; because μ is a probability measure, the event measure is finite.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let ι be a finite nonempty index type and let (Ω, μ) be a probability space. Suppose B i : Ω → Bool is measurable for every i, the whole family (B i)_{i∈ι} is mutually independent under μ, and every B i has the fair Bernoulli law on Bool. Writing n = card ι and counting true as 1 and false as 0, the probability that at least three quarters of the n variables are true is at most exp(-n/8).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is required to be finite by a Fintype instance and explicitly nonempty through 0 < card ι; the theorem does not cover the empty family.
The measure μ is explicitly required to be a probability measure, not merely a finite or arbitrary measure.
Every coordinate B i has an explicit measurability hypothesis; the discrete measurable structure on Bool does not by itself make an arbitrary map out of Ω measurable.
Independence is the indexed mutual-independence predicate for the entire family, which is stronger than merely pairwise independence.
The law hypothesis is exact equality of pushforward measures for every index and fixes both Boolean masses to 1/2.
The summed terms are real-valued Boolean indicators, and card ι is cast to Real before forming the threshold and exponent.

The threshold is the real number (3/4) card ι and the comparison is ≥; because the left side is an integer-valued count, this is equivalently an appropriate ceiling threshold, but no rounding operation occurs in the statement.

The conclusion uses Measure.real, i.e. conversion from an extended nonnegative-real measure value. The probability-measure assumption makes the relevant value finite, so no infinity-collapse issue arises here.

As a universally quantified implication, the proposition would be logically vacuous for any supplied data whose hypotheses were inconsistent, but the displayed assumptions themselves describe an attainable finite family of independent fair Boolean variables.
No converse, matching lower bound, equality case, or claim about thresholds other than three quarters is encoded.
